verdict.rationale: A probe reports an official Groq MCP server documented at console.groq.com/docs/mcp. That could let an AI-native user operate Groq through natural-language commands via an agent, but the evidence does not say what operations it exposes. The remote-MCP and tool-use docs describe Groq models calling external tools, not users controlling Groq itself, so they are not credited. Missing for 10: documented scope of what the MCP server can operate (models, batches, billing, keys), any in-console natural-language command interface, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
